dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: calāsane sthitasyātha śanair vā dehacālanāt | praśānte mānase bhāve devi divyaugham āpnuyāt ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: For one seated on a moving seat, or through slowly rocking the body, as the mind becomes calm, O Goddess, one attains the divine flood.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: seated in a cart, on horseback or on any moving vehicle, the body sways to and fro, or one may sway it oneself; a peculiar joy arises, the mind turns inward and grows calm. He explains divyaugha as the 'divine stream' of wisdom, one of three streams (human, perfected, divine). Wallis: a swing or moving seat, or slow rocking of the body.
dharana.instruction: Rock slowly and gently, or sit on a moving seat, and rest in the calm it brings.

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: A seat that moves gently (a swing, a rocking chair, a passenger seat in a vehicle), or any steady seat in which the body can sway slowly.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 83 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the moving seat or the slowly swaying body
the calm centre of the movement
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a gentle pendulum: the body rocking slowly to and fro, and the stillness that appears in the mind within the movement.
geometry.svg_hint: a soft arc with a still point at its centre
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Rock into calm
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: slow rhythmic rocking soothes the mind until it turns inward and calm. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Let the body rock slowly, or let a moving seat rock it
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.gaze: Eyes closed or soft (open if in a vehicle)
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The slow rocking movement and the calm that grows within it

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: For one seated on a moving seat, or through slowly rocking the body, as the mind becomes calm, O Goddess, one attains the divine flood.
adiyogi.method_summary: Sit on a gently moving seat (a swing, a rocking chair, a passenger seat), or sit still and sway the body slowly and softly to and fro. Let the rhythm calm the mind and rest in that calm.

honesty.disclosure: Door 060 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 60 (verse 83) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 060 is dharana 60, verse 83. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Only as a passenger, never while driving. Keep the movement slow and small; stop if dizzy or queasy. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Breath

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Rock slowly and softly to and fro. Let the rhythm calm the mind. Rest in the calm inside the movement.
